text: We see a significant amount of games. We find engineering teams that are very, very AI forward are reporting about eight to 10 hours save per week.
speaker: Dhanji R. Prasanna
context: Lenny asks about productivity gains from AI, noting there are camps of both AI optimists and skeptics. Dhanji responds with concrete data from Block's experience with AI tools. He explains that AI-forward engineering teams at Block are self-reporting significant time savings, but emphasizes that AI capabilities are rapidly improving, so companies need to continuously adapt and evolve their AI strategies rather than expecting static benefits.
text_ko: 우리는 상당한 수준의 개선 효과를 보고해요. AI 지향(AI-forward)이 강한 엔지니어링 팀(engineering teams)들은 주당 약 8~10시간을 절약한다고 보고해요.
text_zh: 我们看到很多公司都在玩这套。那些在AI方面走得比较前的工程团队反馈说，每周能省下8到10个小时的工作量。
text_es: Vemos muchos casos donde hay juegos importantes. Nos damos cuenta de que los equipos de ingeniería que están muy metidos en IA nos dicen que se están ahorrando entre ocho y diez horas por semana.
key_sentence: engineering teams that are very, very AI forward are reporting about eight to 10 hours save per week.
original_text: We see a significant amount of games. We find engineering teams that are very, very AI forward are reporting about eight to 10 hours save per week. Whenever I hear a stat like this, I think an important element is this is the worst it will ever be. This is now the baseline. The truth is the value is changing every day, so you need to ride that wave along with it.

vocabulary.definition: Having considerable meaning or importance; noteworthy.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'significant' often refers to data or results that have a considerable impact on decision-making or strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'significant' implies importance, it can also suggest a level of quantifiable measurement, making it more suitable in analytical contexts than in casual conversations.

vocabulary.definition: The act of presenting information, often in a structured format, to convey data or findings to stakeholders.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, reporting is crucial for transparency and informed decision-making, often involving financial, operational, or performance metrics.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'reporting' typically implies a formal process, it can also refer to informal updates, but clarity and accuracy are paramount in both contexts.

text: the non-technical people using AI agents and programming tools to build things... are really showing the most impact from these tools.
speaker: Dhanji R. Prasanna
context: Lenny asks which level of engineer benefits most from AI tools - junior or senior engineers. Dhanji reveals a surprising finding that goes against common assumptions. Rather than engineers being the primary beneficiaries, non-technical employees like legal, risk, and support teams are seeing the greatest productivity gains by using AI to build custom software tools for their specific workflows and needs.
text_ko: 실제로 이런 도구들로 가장 큰 효과를 내고 있는 건 기술 전문가는 아니고, AI 에이전트(AI agents)와 프로그래밍 도구(programming tools)를 써서 무언가를 만들어내는 비기술자들이에요.
text_zh: 那些不懂技术的人用AI智能体(AI agents)和编程工具来做东西，反而是从这些工具中获益最大的。
text_es: La gente que no es técnica pero que usa agentes de IA y herramientas de programación para crear cosas... son los que realmente están sacando más provecho de estas herramientas.
key_sentence: the non-technical people using AI agents and programming tools to build things... are really showing the most impact from these tools.
original_text: What's been surprising and really amazing, the non-technical people using AI agents and programming tools to build things, the people that are able to embrace it to optimize for their particular workday and their particular set of tasks are really showing the most impact from these tools.

vocabulary.definition: The strong effect or influence that something has on a situation or individual.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'impact' often refers to the measurable outcomes of initiatives, projects, or tools on productivity, revenue, or user engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'impact' can imply a positive effect, it can also refer to negative consequences, so context is essential when using the term.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to individuals or activities that do not require specialized knowledge in technology or engineering.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, 'non-technical' often describes roles or tasks that focus on management, marketing, or user experience rather than programming or IT skills.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can sometimes carry a connotation of being less sophisticated or knowledgeable in technical matters, so it should be used carefully to avoid undervaluing contributions.

vocabulary.definition: Software applications or platforms that assist developers in writing, testing, and maintaining code.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, programming tools are essential for streamlining development processes, enhancing collaboration, and improving code quality, thereby accelerating product delivery.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'programming tools' typically refer to software, the term can also encompass methodologies and frameworks that facilitate coding, so context is important.

vocabulary.definition: To create or develop something, often referring to the construction of software, products, or systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a startup environment, 'build' is frequently used to describe the process of developing a prototype or product that can be tested and iterated upon based on user feedback.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a hands-on, iterative process, which is often associated with agile methodologies, so it should be used in contexts that emphasize collaboration and flexibility.

text: All these LLMs are sitting idle overnight and on weekends, while humans aren't there. There's no need for that. They should be working all the time. They should be trying to build in anticipation of what we want.
speaker: Dhanji R. Prasanna
context: Lenny asks how Dhanji thinks engineering work will look different in a couple of years. Dhanji envisions a future where AI agents work continuously, not just during human work hours. He describes AI systems that could work overnight and on weekends, proactively building features and solutions in anticipation of human needs, rather than the current model where AI tools only work when humans are actively using them.
text_ko: 대형 언어 모델(LLMs)들이 밤이든 주말이든 사람이 없을 때 가만히 유휴 상태로 있는 건 필요 없어요. 24시간 작동해서 우리가 원할 걸 미리 예측하고 그에 맞춰 계속 뭔가를 만들어내려고 해야 해요.
text_zh: 这些大语言模型(LLM)晚上和周末都闲着，人不在的时候就停工了，完全没必要嘛。应该让它们24小时不停地干活，提前琢磨我们想要什么，把东西准备好。
text_es: Todos estos LLMs se quedan ahí sin hacer nada por las noches y los fines de semana, cuando no está la gente. No tiene sentido. Deberían estar trabajando todo el tiempo. Deberían estar intentando construir cosas anticipándose a lo que queremos.
key_sentence: LLMs should not be sitting idle; they must work in anticipation of our needs.

vocabulary.definition: The act of looking forward to or expecting something to happen in the future.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, anticipation is crucial for strategic planning and forecasting, as it helps organizations prepare for market changes and customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: While anticipation often carries a positive connotation of readiness and foresight, it can also imply anxiety about potential outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: Not active or in use; in a state of inactivity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, idle resources, such as equipment or personnel, represent a missed opportunity for productivity and efficiency, prompting discussions on optimization.
vocabulary.nuance: Idle can carry a negative connotation, suggesting wastefulness, but it may also imply a necessary pause for maintenance or strategic reflection.

text: A lot of engineers think that code quality is important to building a successful product. The two have nothing to do with each other.
speaker: Dhanji R. Prasanna
context: Lenny asks about the most counterintuitive lesson Dhanji has learned about building products or teams. Dhanji challenges a core belief held by many engineers about the relationship between code quality and product success. This statement goes against conventional software engineering wisdom that emphasizes clean, well-architected code as essential for product success.
text_ko: 많은 엔지니어들이 코드 품질(code quality)이 성공적인 제품을 만드는 데 중요하다고 생각해요. 그런데 사실 둘은 전혀 상관없어요.
text_zh: 很多工程师都觉得代码质量对做出成功产品很重要。其实这俩压根儿就没什么关系。
text_es: Muchos ingenieros creen que la calidad del código es clave para construir un producto exitoso. En realidad, una cosa no tiene nada que ver with la otra.
key_sentence: Code quality and building a successful product have nothing to do with each other.

vocabulary.definition: A product that meets market needs effectively, resulting in high customer satisfaction and strong sales performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech companies, the definition of a successful product often includes metrics such as user engagement, profitability, and market share.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'successful product' generally implies positive outcomes, it can also be context-dependent, varying by industry and target audience.

text: So everything from getting the top ICs in the company together to talk to each other, to starting a whole bunch of special projects. So we got about two to five engineers per project.
speaker: Dhanji R. Prasanna
context: Lenny asks about the bigger changes Dhanji made after getting executive buy-in for his AI manifesto. Dhanji explains his strategy for transforming Block back into a technology-first company. He describes implementing several programs designed to reignite the engineering culture, including bringing together top individual contributors (ICs), launching multiple small experimental projects, and restarting company-wide hackathons to create momentum around building innovative technology.
text_ko: 그래서 회사 내 최고의 IC들(top ICs)을 모아 서로 대화하게 하는 것부터, 특별 프로젝트를 여러 개 시작하는 것까지 다 했어요. 각 프로젝트당 엔지니어는 보통 2명에서 5명 정도였어요.
text_zh: 所以我们做了很多事情，比如把公司里最厉害的IC(individual contributor)都聚到一起互相交流，还启动了一大堆特殊项目。每个项目大概配2到5个工程师。
text_es: Entonces todo, desde juntar a los mejores ingenieros individuales (top ICs) de la empresa para que hablen entre ellos, hasta arrancar un montón de proyectos especiales. Así que tenemos entre dos y cinco ingenieros por proyecto.
key_sentence: So we got about two to five engineers per project.
original_text: So everything from getting the top ICs in the company together to talk to each other, to starting a whole bunch of special projects. So we got about two to five engineers per project. There were about eight or nine different projects and we had reinstituted, the company-wide hack week.

text: I think that one of the things that I learned the most throughout this process is that Conway's Law can be really, really powerful. So it's the law that basically says you ship your org structure.
speaker: Dhanji R. Prasanna
context: Lenny asks how Block's engineering teams work differently today versus a few years ago. Dhanji reflects on the organizational transformation from GM structure to functional structure and explains a key insight he gained. Conway's Law states that organizations design systems that mirror their communication structure - meaning the way teams are organized directly influences the products they create. This was a crucial realization in Block's transformation to become more technically focused.
text_ko: 제가 이 과정을 통해 가장 많이 배운 것 중 하나는 콘웨이 법칙(Conway's Law)이 정말, 정말 강력하다는 거예요. 이 법칙은 결국 조직 구조(org structure)가 그대로 결과물에 반영된다는 뜻이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得这整个过程中学到最多的一点就是，康威定律(Conway's Law)真的非常厉害。这个定律说的就是，你的产品结构基本上就是你组织架构的翻版。
text_es: Creo que una de las cosas que más aprendí en todo este proceso es que la Ley de Conway puede ser tremendamente poderosa. Básicamente es la ley que dice que al final terminas enviando tu estructura organizacional.
key_sentence: Conway's Law shows you ship your org structure, impacting what you build.
original_text: I think that one of the things that I learned the most throughout this process is that Conway's Law can be really, really powerful. So it's the law that basically says you ship your org structure. So what you're organized as in terms of teams, in terms of collaborating groups and your operating model matters a lot to what you build.

vocabulary.definition: Having great strength or influence; capable of producing significant effects or results.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, something described as powerful may refer to a strategy, tool, or individual that can drive substantial change or impact within an organization.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'powerful' can denote effectiveness, it may also imply a sense of authority or dominance that could be perceived negatively in collaborative environments.

vocabulary.businessContext: A well-defined structure is crucial for ensuring clear communication, delineating responsibilities, and facilitating decision-making processes in a business environment.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'structure' typically has a neutral connotation, it can imply rigidity or inflexibility if not designed to adapt to changing circumstances.
